category_title: Young autistic children in early language learning stages who engage in sequentially organized play
minimal_context: The student and tutor are playing with a slinky at a table during a free-play session to practice interactional turn-taking.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's play with the slinky on the table.

STUDENT: (Extends the slinky in and out while gazing at it.)

TUTOR: You got the slinky. (Moves hand toward the slinky)

STUDENT: (Moves the slinky toward you but holds onto it.)

TUTOR: Can I see the slinky? (Holds hand out)

STUDENT: (Steps back, places the slinky on the table instead of handing it directly, and releases it while gazing at it.)

options.A: Apply protective procedures noncontingently across all conditions and for the entirety of the free-play session (e.g., adding canvas sleeves).
options.B: Use the word "look" to signal an upcoming demonstration or change in the slinky play activity.
options.C: Provide a visual chart with everyone's name, date, and time, and announce the 15-minute duration at the beginning of the session.
options.D: Allow the student to keep the slinky under the condition that they do not show it to others, and break off the session.
